claims.content: To allow Field Maintenance Staff to diagnose and identify the cause of a device failure by accessing diagnostic commands, viewing device status, and reviewing alarm or fault data recorded in the system.

goal.raw_text: To allow Field Maintenance Staff to diagnose and identify the cause of a device failure by accessing diagnostic commands, viewing device status, and reviewing alarm or fault data recorded in the system.

claims.content: Field Maintenance Staff
The system is operating in a mode that supports maintenance activities (e.g., 'Maintenance' mode).
The target device is registered in the system database with defined attributes (Device ID, Name, Category, etc.).
The Field Maintenance Staff member has valid personnel credentials (Personnel ID, Classification) to access the system.
The system supports 'Diagnostic Commands' which allow running diagnostics on communication cards or controllers.
A device failure is detected by the system or reported to Field Maintenance Staff, prompting the need to run diagnostic commands on the affected device.

trigger.raw_text: A device failure is detected by the system or reported to Field Maintenance Staff, prompting the need to run diagnostic commands on the affected device.

claims.content: Field Maintenance Staff accesses the system and selects the failed device from the registered devices list.
Staff initiates a 'Diagnostic Command' on the selected device to run diagnostics on its communication card or controller.
System executes the diagnostic command and returns status or fault data for the device.
System logs the diagnostic command execution and result in the Device Command Log and System Operations Command Log.
Field Maintenance Staff reviews the returned diagnostic data, alarm criteria, and device state to identify the root cause of failure.
If the diagnostic command fails to execute or returns an error, the system shall record the failure in the Device Command Log and System Operations Command Log.
If the device remains in an unknown state after diagnostics, the system shall not complete the command change for that device and shall not send a device command to the field device.
If the Field Maintenance Staff lacks valid personnel credentials or classification level required to access the device or run diagnostics, the system shall deny access to the diagnostic function.
If the target device is not registered in the system database (i.e., no Device ID, Name, Category, etc.), the system shall not allow selection of the device for diagnosis.
If the system is not in a mode that supports maintenance activities (e.g., not in 'Maintenance' mode), diagnostic commands may be restricted or unavailable to Field Maintenance Staff.
If the device remains in an unknown state, the system shall not complete the command change for that device and shall not send a device command to the field device.
If the Field Maintenance Staff lacks valid personnel credentials or classification level required to access the device or run diagnostics, the system shall deny access to the diagnostic function.
If the target device is not registered in the system database (i.e., no Device ID, Name, Category, etc.), the system shall not allow selection of the device for diagnosis.
If the system is not in a mode that supports maintenance activities (e.g., not in 'Maintenance' mode), diagnostic commands may be restricted or unavailable to Field Maintenance Staff.
The diagnostic command execution and its result are logged in the Device Command Log.
The diagnostic command execution and its result are logged in the System Operations Command Log.
If the device remains in an unknown state after diagnostics, no device command is sent to the field device.
The system maintains a record of the diagnostic outcome for audit and historical transaction reporting purposes.
